what: Tri City provides free medical and dental services to uninsured Central Kane residents. Original 2024 Form 990 identifies EIN 36-4475369, resolving the malformed number previously displayed on its site without inventing a digit.
Illustrative central annual Chicago-MSA QALYs: 1.731300; model assumptions are uncalibrated.

sections.what: Tri City provides free medical and dental services to uninsured Central Kane residents. Original 2024 Form 990 identifies EIN 36-4475369, resolving the malformed number previously displayed on its site without inventing a digit.
sections.monitoring: Original FY2024 return reports 580 unique medical patients, 3,390 medical visits, 3,546 medications and 607 dental visits. Only the unique medical patient count enters the benefit model; dental, tests and prescriptions are not added as separate people. No causal change in patient health utility is reported.
sections.qualitative: Medical and dental access may improve pain, function and disease management. The central pathway models medical morbidity relief and assigns unmodeled dental or other health provisionally zero net QALYs, not a proven lower bound. The full cost numerator retains dental and other programs. Volunteer capacity and other care options may reduce additionality.
sections.cost: Schedule D reconciles audited expense $1,379,104 to Form 990 expense $938,094 through $441,010 of donated services/use of facilities. Central gross cost restores $6,552 direct event expense netted from revenue: $1,385,656. This addback is a modeling boundary choice; no-addback sensitivity uses $1,379,104. Noncash goods already recognized in the return are not added again.
sections.funding: Original FY2024 return reports revenue $1,128,821 and net assets $1,317,382. Schedule D audited revenue is $1,589,022. An audit-expense reconciliation is available, but the complete audit and resource valuation methods were not inspected. No priced marginal expansion plan establishes what another gift buys.

model.counterfactual: a is the share with meaningful morbidity relief beyond equivalent alternative care; b separately discounts replacement funding and constrained volunteer capacity. No mortality benefit is credited.
model.attribution: One morbidity pathway only. Other health pathways are provisionally assigned zero net benefit, not demonstrated zero or a lower bound. Visits, prescriptions and retail care values are not added as QALYs. Cross-recipient benefits cannot be summed without person-level deduplication.
model.uncertainty: All utility, causal response, duration, funding additionality and residence parameters are illustrative judgments, not measured causal effects, calibrated expected values, confidence intervals or marginal gift purchase prices. Different accounting treatment of donated care prevents comparative economic-efficiency rankings.
sensitivity: Poor and favorable scenarios vary several uncalibrated assumptions together; they are not exhaustive bounds.
Zero additionality produces zero QALYs and no finite price.
Changing cost alone scales price proportionally; changing any multiplicative benefit factor inversely scales price.
No event addback lowers cost by $6,552. Do not add dental patients without deduplication.
missingInputs: Recipient causal morbidity and health-utility outcomes with follow-up and alternative-care comparison.
Additional unrestricted dollars, priced unfunded expansion and binding staff/volunteer constraints.
Patient residence, overlap across services and clinics, and incremental economic cost of donated resources.
Direct complete audit and in-kind valuation methods.
model.costScope: Whole recipient gross accounting cost: audited expense including recognized donated services plus netted direct event expense. Not medical-program expense alone. Unrecognized resources and true opportunity costs are unresolved.
model.geographicAttribution: Primary mission limits care to Central Kane County; St Charles clinic is within Kane and the pinned 13-county Chicago MSA. g=.995 is a judged residence share allowing exceptions, not a patient-level measurement.
model.nativeOutcomes: FY2024: 580 unique medical patients, 3,390 medical visits and 607 dental visits; only the first is modeled as persons.

scenarios.label: Illustrative central
scenarios.assumptions: N=580; k=1; a=.30; u=.05; T=.5; b=.4; g=0.995. Judged benefit conversion, not measured EV.

scenarios.label: Illustrative poor case
scenarios.assumptions: k=0.5; a=.1; u=.02; T=.25; b=.2; g=.9. No probability assigned.

scenarios.label: Illustrative favorable case
scenarios.assumptions: k=1; a=.5; u=.08; T=1; b=.7; g=1. Not an upper bound.

scenarios.label: No additional health benefit
scenarios.assumptions: b=0: all care replaced or constrained; zero benefit, no finite price.

scenarios.label: Audited net-event accounting boundary
scenarios.assumptions: Same benefit assumptions; audited expense without restoring $6,552 netted event cost.
